measurement_basis: authenticated prior authority-denial evidence, current repository guidance, and the newly established campaign session

observation.source_interface: MNCS Environment authority guidance, session events, and capability projection

outcome.observed_limit: At the repository baseline, README.md and RFC 0002 described merge and publish as persistent-claim-required even though the executable authority policy and docs/ENTRY.md allowed scoped integration without a claim. Recorded authority events also lacked campaign and WorkIntent references, so the projection could not directly relate a denial to the objective it interrupted.
outcome.current_observation: A real merge preflight in the new campaign session was allowed without an owned persistent claim. The projection linked it to campaign cmp_7cee66bc5d834dad and WorkIntent int_e9a2959ffe2e952c, and retained 25 observed claim overlaps with truncation explicit.
outcome.analysis_limit: The prior denial is authentic evidence from an earlier session, but it does not establish a live concurrent owner at denial time. The current preflight establishes eligibility only; no Git merge or publication was executed.

pressure_hypothesis.title: Authority guidance and event evidence do not consistently expose claim-free integration under its motivating objective
pressure_hypothesis.subsystem: MNCS Environment authority policy, documentation, and session activity projection
pressure_hypothesis.basis: The prior campaign recorded an overlapping-claim merge denial. At the implementation baseline, top-level guidance still required a persistent claim for merge and publish despite the live policy allowing exact-scope integration without one. Neither the earlier denial nor preflight event carried the WorkIntent reference needed to correlate authority friction with its objective.
pressure_hypothesis.actionable_recommendation: Keep canonical guidance aligned with executable eligibility rules and attach stable campaign and WorkIntent references to authority observations so projections can relate coordination pressure to the objective affected.
